content.text: Eduversal Partner Schools are committed to leveraging technology to enhance teaching and learning, prepare students for success in a digital world, and develop responsible digital citizens. Technology serves as a tool to support pedagogical goals, not as an end in itself. All technology integration must demonstrate clear educational benefit and align with the school's Schoolwide Learner Outcomes (SLOs), particularly Innovation and Communication.
content.title: 21.1.1 Vision Statement
21.1.2 Strategic Objectives
content.text: The Digital Learning Strategy aims to achieve the following objectives over a 3-5 year horizon:

items: **Teaching and Learning Enhancement:** Integrate technology meaningfully into curriculum delivery to personalize learning, increase engagement, support diverse learners (including EAL students), and develop 21st-century skills aligned with Cambridge International standards and Indonesian national curriculum requirements.

**Infrastructure Development:** Maintain robust, reliable, and secure IT infrastructure that supports teaching and learning activities, administrative operations, and communication needs across all school contexts (day schools, boarding schools, urban and rural settings).

**Digital Literacy and Citizenship:** Develop students' digital literacy skills and responsible technology use, preparing them to be ethical and effective digital citizens who understand online safety, privacy, and the responsible use of emerging technologies including artificial intelligence.

**Staff Professional Development:** Build staff capacity to integrate technology effectively through ongoing professional development aligned with Cambridge's professional development pathways, including "Getting Started with AI in the Classroom" and "Teaching with Technology" modules.

**Data Security and Privacy:** Protect student, staff, and institutional data through robust cybersecurity measures, compliance with Indonesian data protection regulations (UU PDP), and adherence to Cambridge secure materials handling requirements.

content.text: Digital learning initiatives are embedded within the School Improvement Plan (SIP) and monitored through EduNav dashboards. Technology-related KPIs are tracked as part of the school appraisal process under Domain 4: Educational Resources and Technology. Cross-Reference: See Section 4 for Strategic Planning and School Improvement framework.
content.title: 21.1.3 Alignment with School Improvement

subsections.title: EduNav Platform: School Information System and Learning Management System

content.text: EduNav is the integrated School Information System (SIS) and Learning Management System (LMS) deployed across all Eduversal Partner Schools. Developed and maintained by PT. Global Zerone Digital (Zerone), EduNav serves as the central digital platform for school operations, teaching delivery, and stakeholder communication. EduNav provides accounts for students, teachers, staff, and parents with customized access to relevant educational services. The platform supports student information management, learning evaluations, attendance tracking, grading, scheduling, and school administration.
content.title: 21.2.1 Overview of EduNav

content.text: Student Information System (SIS) Functions:

items: Student enrollment and registration management
Attendance tracking and absence reporting
Gradebook and academic record management
Scheduling and timetable management
Parent communication and notification systems
Administrative reporting and data analytics
Integration with Indonesian Dapodik requirements
content.title: 21.2.2 Core Functions

content.text: Learning Management System (LMS) Functions:

items: Course content organization and delivery
Assignment creation, submission, and feedback
Online quizzes and assessments
Discussion forums and collaborative tools
Resource library and digital content repository
Progress tracking and learning analytics
Communication tools (announcements, messaging)

content.title: 21.2.3 User Access and Roles
content.text: EduNav implements role-based access control to ensure users can only access information appropriate to their role:

items: **Students:** Access to personal academic records, course materials, assignments, grades, attendance records, and communication tools. Students can submit work, take part in discussions, and view feedback.

**Teachers:** Access to class rosters, gradebook functionality, course management tools, communication features, and student academic information for assigned classes. EduNav-LMS is the primary platform for lesson delivery. Approved third-party tools (see 21.9.1) complement it; they do not replace it. Tools outside the approved list require approval under 21.9.3.

**Parents/Guardians:** Access to their child's academic progress, grades, attendance, behavior records, and school communications. Parents receive automated notifications for significant assessments and communications.
**School Administrators:** Full access to administrative functions, reporting tools, and system configuration. Access to student records is governed by need-to-know principles.
**Eduversal Central:** Oversight access for quality assurance, appraisal data, and network-wide reporting while respecting data protection requirements.

content.text: Teachers have specific responsibilities for effective use of the LMS:

items: Maintain current and organized course content aligned with curriculum standards
Provide clear directions and instructions when sharing materials
Update gradebook regularly with assessment results and feedback
Encourage students to use comment features for communication
Respond to student queries within reasonable timeframes
take part in training programs for LMS usage
Report technical issues promptly to IT support

content.title: 21.5.4 Cyberbullying Prevention and Response

content.text: Response:

items: Report to homeroom teacher, counselor, or SC Coordinator

Investigation following discipline procedures

Consequences for perpetrators (minimum Level 3)
Parent notification for all parties
Documentation and monitoring

content.text: Cross-Reference: See Section 9.6 for cyberbullying within safeguarding framework; Section 22.8.1 for anti-bullying policy.

content.title: Limits on monitoring student devices and activity
items: Purpose limitation: monitoring data is collected only for safeguarding and for enforcing the Acceptable Use Policy. It is not used for any other purpose.
Retention: browsing logs for managed devices are retained for 90 days and then deleted, unless retained longer as part of a specific safeguarding record.

Scope: monitoring is active during school hours and on school networks. Take-home devices are not monitored outside school hours except where a live safeguarding concern requires it, authorised by the Principal.

Notice: students and parents are told in plain language, at enrolment and annually, what is monitored, why, how long it is kept, and who can see it. Monitoring that has not been notified is not permitted.
Proportionality: these limits implement UU No. 27/2022 (purpose limitation and data minimisation) and PP No. 17/2025 (risk assessment and protection of minors' data).

content.text: Password Requirements:

Passwords are changed on suspected compromise, not on a fixed schedule (scheduled rotation is deprecated by NIST SP 800-63B because it drives predictable, weaker passwords). Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all administrator accounts

Eduversal recognizes artificial intelligence as an emerging tool that can significantly enhance teaching and learning when used ethically and responsibly. AI should complement, not replace, quality teaching and genuine student learning. The school's approach to AI balances embracing beneficial applications with maintaining academic integrity and safeguarding student development.
content.title: 21.8.1 Vision for AI in Education

content.text: For Teachers:

items: Lesson planning assistance and resource creation
Differentiation and personalization support
Administrative task automation (with appropriate review)
Assessment design (not for grading without teacher review)
Professional learning and research
Communication drafting (with appropriate review)
content.title: 21.8.2 Permitted Uses of AI

content.text: Teachers must always review and verify AI-generated content before use with students. For Students (When Explicitly Permitted by Teacher):

items: Research assistance and information synthesis
Brainstorming and idea generation
Revision and study support
Language learning assistance (for EAL students)
Creative inspiration (not final submission)
Coding assistance for technology projects

content.text: For Students:

items: Submitting AI-generated work as own work without disclosure
Using AI during assessments unless explicitly permitted
Bypassing learning processes through AI dependence
Using AI to complete homework or assignments intended for independent completion
Using AI to take tests or complete controlled assessments
content.title: 21.8.3 Prohibited Uses of AI

content.text: For Staff:

items: Writing student reports without substantial personal input
Grading student work entirely by AI without review
Making important decisions affecting students based solely on AI recommendations
Using AI that processes student personal data without proper authorization

content.text: When AI use is permitted:

items: Students must acknowledge AI assistance in their work
Description of how AI was used (research, drafting, editing, etc.)
All final work must reflect student's own understanding and voice
Original thinking and critical analysis must be demonstrated
content.title: 21.8.4 Disclosure Requirements

content.text: Failure to disclose AI assistance constitutes academic dishonesty.
Teachers receive professional development on AI integration aligned with Cambridge's "Getting Started with AI in the Classroom" workshop:

items: Understanding foundational AI concepts

Ethical considerations and best practices
Creating AI-enhanced educational environments

content.text: Students learn about AI through age-appropriate instruction:

items: Understanding what AI is and how it works
Recognizing AI in everyday life
Critical evaluation of AI-generated content
Ethical considerations and limitations
Future implications and career relevance

content.text: The relationship between AI and academic integrity is addressed through:

items: Clear policy communication to students and parents
Age-appropriate discussions about learning value
Assessment design that maintains integrity
Detection and response procedures

content.title: 21.8.6 Academic Integrity and AI

content.text: Cross-Reference: See Section 6.4 for academic integrity; Section 22.8.2 for AI-related misconduct consequences.

content.title: AI and safeguarding - harms, not just academic integrity
items: Synthetic sexual imagery. Creating, requesting, sharing, or possessing AI-generated sexual or "nudified" images of any student or staff member is a Level 4 safeguarding matter. It is referred to the DSL immediately and handled under Section 9, never as an ordinary conduct matter under Section 22. Where the subject is a child, this may constitute a criminal offence.

Deepfake harassment. AI-generated images, audio, or video used to humiliate, impersonate, or threaten a member of the school community is treated as digital kekerasan under Permendikdasmen No. 6/2026 (BSAN), which names "digital" as one of its six forms of violence.

AI companions and chatbots. Students may form sustained relationships with AI companion applications. Staff who become aware of a student relying on an AI companion for emotional support refer the concern to the school counsellor.
AI-enabled grooming. Staff safeguarding training covers how AI tools can be used to generate convincing false identities and to scale grooming attempts.

Age-appropriate design. Any AI tool approved for student use must be age-appropriate for the year group, must not target advertising at minors, and must not train on student data. This test is applied in the app-approval process at 21.9.3 and is not optional.
Anchors: PP No. 17/2025 (PP Tunas), Permendikdasmen No. 6/2026 (BSAN), and the 5Rights Children and AI Design Code (2025).

content.title: 21.9.4 LMS-First Approach

content.text: This policy applies to all students, teachers, staff, parents, guardians, volunteers, and anyone representing the school in any official capacity on social media platforms, whether on-campus or off-campus.
content.title: 21.10.1 Scope

content.text: Respect and Civility: Students must maintain respectful and civil conduct when using social media. Cyberbullying, harassment, and hate speech will not be tolerated and will be addressed through discipline procedures. Privacy: Students must protect their own and others' privacy by not sharing personal information such as addresses, phone numbers, or private details on social media. Academic Integrity: Students must uphold academic integrity and avoid using social media for cheating, plagiarism, or any form of academic dishonesty. School Representation: Students should be mindful that their online behavior reflects on the school community, particularly when identifiable through uniforms, school names, or location tags.
content.title: 21.10.2 Student Use of Social Media

content.text: Professionalism: Teachers and staff must maintain high professionalism when using social media. Personal opinions expressed online should be clearly distinguished from school positions. Privacy and Confidentiality: Staff must protect the privacy and confidentiality of students, colleagues, and the school. No sensitive or private information should be shared. Boundaries: Staff must avoid forming personal relationships with students on social media platforms. Communication with students should primarily occur through official school channels (EduNav, school email). Images and Content: Staff must not post photos or videos of students without proper consent and must follow school media consent procedures.
content.title: 21.10.3 Staff Use of Social Media

content.text: Account Ownership: Official school social media accounts are owned and managed by the school. Only authorized staff members should have access to these accounts. Content Guidelines: All content shared on official school social media accounts should:

items: Align with the school's values, mission, and policies
Be approved by designated authority before posting
Comply with media consent requirements
Present the school positively and professionally
Avoid controversial or divisive content
content.title: 21.10.4 Official School Accounts

content.text: Monitoring: Official accounts should be monitored regularly for comments and interactions requiring response or moderation.

content.title: Indonesian regulations governing digital learning and child online protection
items: UU No. 27/2022 concerning Personal Data Protection (UU PDP) - lawful basis, purpose limitation, data-subject rights, and breach notification within 3x24 hours (Article 46(1)). Section 14 is the controlling text.

PP No. 17/2025 concerning Tata Kelola Penyelenggaraan Sistem Elektronik dalam Pelindungan Anak ("PP Tunas"), effective 1 April 2025 - the framework regulation for child protection in electronic systems. It requires age verification, tiered parental consent for users under 17, content filtering, risk assessment, and protection of minors' images and data. School WiFi filtering and student-device policy sit under this instrument.
Permen Komdigi No. 9/2026 - the implementing regulation for PP Tunas.
Sector lead: Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital (Komdigi), formerly Kemkominfo.

Permendikdasmen No. 6/2026 (BSAN) - note that BSAN includes "digital" as one of its six forms of kekerasan, so online harm between students is a safeguarding matter under Section 9 as well as a conduct matter under Section 22.
